title: Upgrade Safeguard Index & Provider Stability Catalog for Private VPC IaC
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Purpose:
Create a machine-readable compatibility index and human-facing catalog that prescribes pinned provider/module versions, upgrade windows, and automated health checks for Private (VPC) deployments. The index will drive CI gating, an upgrade dashboard, and an automated rollback/mitigation playbook. This ticket covers: scope, recommended pin policy, a compatibility matrix for the most-used providers/modules in our Private stacks, CI checks to prevent accidental incompatible upgrades, and the initial runbook for upgrade-day failures.

Scope (what this ticket delivers):
- A canonical CSV/JSON compatibility index checked into infra/compat/ (TF core + provider + module compatibility lines).
- A small service (scripts + GitHub Actions) that regenerates provider-lock and verifies plan/apply in a canary workspace.
- Documentation page (Console -> Private IaC -> Upgrade Index) and a README describing pinning rationale.
- Rollback & mitigation playbook steps embedded into the index file and surfaced in the Console runbook.

Design principles / decisions:
- Pin majors tightly for providers with breaking changes, allow conservative minor ranges only when provider changelogs guarantee backward compatibility.
- Use provider lockfile (terraform.lock.hcl) as source-of-truth for patch pins; index recommends allowed major.minor ranges.
- Record a stability_score per provider (A/B/C) but keep score as doc guidance, not an enforcement gate.
- Automate compatibility checks in PRs: terraform init -upgrade=false, terraform providers mirror, run our compat-test (see CI checklist below).

Compatibility Matrix (summary - canonical CSV will be added to infra/compat/compat-index.csv):
- Terraform Core: 1.5.x -> Supported baseline for all private stacks. Recommended test runner: 1.5.7 for CI.
- hashicorp/aws provider: recommended range 5.18.x <= v < 6.0.0; lock to exact patch in terraform.lock.hcl. Notes: v6 introduces breaking changes to IAM policy document serialization; treat v6 as major upgrade. Stability_score: A.
- hashicorp/kubernetes provider: recommended range 2.14.x <= v < 3.0.0; pin to >=2.14.3 for k8s v1.28 compatibility. Stability_score: B.
- hashicorp/helm provider: recommended range 2.7.x <= v < 3.0.0; pin >=2.7.1 due to API renames for chart dependency. Stability_score: B.
- hashicorp/random, null, tls: stay on 3.x/4.x families; these are low-risk but pin to exact patch in lockfile. Stability_score: A.
- registry.redwood/module/private-vpc: module semantic versioning policy: patch/backward-compatible bugfixes only on same minor. We require module-major.minor to be pinned in root modules; allow patch upgrades automatically.

Recommended pin policy (applied as CI rules):
1) Add provider version constraints in module's required_providers and in root stacks. Use >=minor.patch, <next_major for allowed range.
2) Commit terraform.lock.hcl to repo and do NOT allow terraform init -upgrade in CI without an explicit upgrade PR.
3) Add a pre-merge CI job that runs terraform init && terraform providers lock && terraform plan using the pinned lockfile. Any diff in providers triggers an "upgrade proposal" PR with autogenerated changelog snippets.

Automated checks to add to CI (initial list):
- compat-check: validates the PR's provider constraints against compat-index.csv and fails if outside allowed range.
- smoke-canary: runs 'terraform plan' in a canary workspace using the same stack inputs as production but taped to short-lived resources; failure flags the PR.
- e2e-kv-cache: light-weight infra smoke to exercise KV cache creation in a canary network (ensures modules' provider APIs are functional).

Rollback & Mitigation Playbook (high-level):
1) Detection: Console alerts -> infra-alert channel + page duty. Run 'compat-health-check' script to gather providers and module versions across private clusters.
2) Short-term mitigation: route traffic away from affected region/pool (smart routing). If change is config-only, re-apply previous commit (git revert + terraform apply in rollback workspace).
3) Provider revert: if provider upgrade caused plan failures post-apply, pin provider version to previous patch and apply (requires lockfile update + apply).
4) If module introduced state drift: execute targeted state-file remediation (state mv/import) following module author guidance; escalate to SRE.
5) Postmortem: collect logs, attach failing terraform plan, provider changelog link, and the compat-index line that allowed the upgrade.

Acceptance criteria (must be met before closing):
- compat-index.csv and compat-index.json committed under infra/compat with at least the providers/modules listed above.
- CI jobs implemented and green in a test repo (compat-check + smoke-canary).
- Runbook added to docs/infrastructure/upgrade-index.md and linked from Console runbook.
- A canary upgrade executed end-to-end for aws provider minor bump (5.19.x) documented with results.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How aggressively should we block minors vs. allow them with canary? Current proposal: allow minor within same major only after successful canary. This risks delay but reduces incidents.
- Do we expose stability_score to customers in Console? Prefer internal-only for first iteration.
